data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's installation process changes the subject's environment so that failures the test was designed to catch are masked before the test can observe them.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation lost under compile.py was due to a different cause than shown-to-fail-first installation (e.g., a pre-existing bug in the mutation itself), then the constraint-vs-description distinction collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 distribution can be explained by a known, documented weakness in the mutation-testing tool rather than by the test's installation procedure, then the claim is false.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an independent re-run of the same mutation under a clean installation catches all 9/9, then the shown-to-fail-first installation was not the constraining mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In the shown-to-fail-first installation, the compiler's own mutations (1/9 lost under compile.py) were hidden because the test harness was installed in a state that already contained the failure signature. The test then verifies the installed state rather than the subject's independent behavior, making the test a constraint that constructs the subject it purports to describe. The 3-of-26 result follows from the distribution: every ordinarily-guarded module showed 4/4 to 6/7 mutations caught, but the one mutation lost under fail-first installation slipped through because the guard that would catch it was never exercised in the installed configuration.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
